test.name: Pre-adoption Catholic Europe date — no Gregorian equivalent existed yet
test.description: User asks to convert a Madrid parish date of '14 September 1582' to Gregorian. Spain's switch was Julian 4 October 1582 -> Gregorian 15 October 1582, so this date PRECEDES the Gregorian calendar's existence: there is no contemporaneous Gregorian equivalent, only a proleptic one. The skill should say so and record the date as written rather than asserting a converted day as fact. convert_calendar is specified to reject julianToGregorianDay before 1582-10-15 as an input error (convert-calendar-tool-spec.md section 7), so a bare '24 September 1582' is an answer the tool will not produce. The 10-day offset band itself is exercised by ut_convert_dates_009 (Wuerttemberg 1699).

input.user_message: Convert this Spanish parish-record date to the modern Gregorian calendar: '14 September 1582, Madrid'.

judge_context: Should recognize that Spain adopted the Gregorian calendar in October 1582 — Julian 4 October was followed directly by Gregorian 15 October — so a 14 September 1582 Madrid date is Julian and sits BEFORE the switch

Should explain that because the date precedes the Gregorian calendar's introduction, there is no contemporaneous Gregorian equivalent to convert to. The calendars had not yet diverged into two parallel systems; before 15 October 1582 there was only the Julian calendar
Should recommend recording the date as written — '14 September 1582' — with the calendar noted (Julian / Old Style), which is what another researcher will be able to match against the register

May state the proleptic Gregorian alignment (24 September 1582) for timeline comparison, but ONLY labelled as proleptic or hypothetical. Presenting '24 September 1582' flatly as the Gregorian date, with no indication that the Gregorian calendar did not exist on that day, is the failure this test looks for

If the skill calls convert_calendar with julianToGregorianDay and receives an input error, surfacing that error and explaining it is correct behaviour, not a failure — the tool rejects this correction before 1582-10-15 by design
